statement.p: Build a spreadsheet that computes the difference between f(x) and L(x) for x-values between -1 and 1\text{,} spaced 0.1 units apart. Note: we will revisit this spreadsheet for additional computations in Activity8.1.12, so it would be ideal if you save your work electronically in place you can find it later.

Next, add a column to your spreadsheet that computes \lvert f(x)-L(x)\rvert\text{.} What is the new entry in Row 14?
How do the differences between f(x) and L(x) change as you move across the interval from -1 to 1\text{?}

li.p: Differences get larger the farther away x is from 0.

statement.p: For about what values of x is it true that \lvert f(x) - L(x)\rvert \lt 0.1\text{?}
Notice that the curvature in f(x) = e^x is what makes the linear approximation L(x) lose accuracy. What kind of simple function might do a better job approximating e^x than a linear one?
